clue.text: Potential opener, one that may yet represent Yorkshire

definitions.meaning: a bud is a flower that has not yet opened but will

definitions.text: one that may yet represent Yorkshire
definitions.meaning: the white rose is Yorkshire's emblem, so an unopened rose may one day stand for the county

explanation.surface: A cricket selector eyes a promising young opening batsman who may yet play for Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests cricket, where Yorkshire is a famous county side; in fact it is a flower that opens, and Yorkshire's emblem is the white rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is an unopened flower bud, something that will open in time and grow into the county's emblem.

clue.text: Healthy transport in decay

indicators.note: in places the transport word inside the word for decay

parts.note: decay means rot
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: A remark that public transport is in a sorry state but still somehow sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone robust is strong and in good health.

clue.text: Mother's coming up on a vessel — a Chinese one

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: mother is MA, with the possessive S
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Mum is boarding a boat in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in the definition stands for 'vessel', so the definition is a Chinese vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in China and East Asia, so it is a Chinese vessel.

clue.text: Man of the match?

parts.note: a match is also a marriage, and the main man at a wedding is the groom

explanation.surface: Who was the star player of the game?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the match' is the award for the best player in a sports game; here the match is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The man getting married is the male half of a matrimonial match.

clue.text: Doctor and a graduate join together in play

parts.note: MA, a Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A doctor and a graduate team up to act in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a drama is a play written for the stage.

clue.text: Seems in order to get retribution

indicators.note: putting letters in order means rearranging them, signalling an anagram of the words before it

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Things seem to be set right when payback arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like a phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder: SEEMS IN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is the goddess of vengeance, and the word means just punishment or retribution.

clue.text: Clothing range with buckles

indicators.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A clothing line with fasteners on every garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckles' looks like the plural noun for belt fasteners; it is a verb, bending the letters of RANGE WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is the clothing worn in bed, such as pyjamas and nightdresses.

clue.text: Repair men do nothing less

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: less means without, so the zero letter is taken away from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Fix it: the men are doing less than nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mend something is to repair it.

clue.text: Basic requirements for ship launchings

parts.note: ships are built on sloping ramps down which they slide into the water at launch

explanation.surface: What you need to launch a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipways are the inclined ramps from which a newly built vessel slides into the water.

clue.text: Those resting between the lines?

parts.note: people asleep are resting, and railway ties lie between the rails

explanation.surface: People taking a nap in the space between written lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The beams supporting a railway track are called this in Britain (ties in the US); they lie across the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means people who sleep and also the beams laid under railway tracks.

clue.text: Animated youngster in film and book given limited scope

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the last letter is taken off the synonym

parts.note: ambit means scope or extent

explanation.surface: A cartoon youngster from a film and book that has only narrow range.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the young deer who stars in the animated Disney film based on Felix Salten's book.

clue.text: Entering ground, following a South American

indicators.note: following places the rearranged word after the letter A
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of the word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moves onto the land after a South American.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentine is a term for a person from Argentina, a South American country.

clue.text: Uncast replacements?

parts.note: roles in a play nobody has been cast in are parts left over, and replacements for machines are spares

explanation.surface: Understudies standing by for roles not yet filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare parts are replacement components; read as theatre, they are roles that remain unassigned.

clue.text: Exchange prisoners of war in turn

indicators.note: turning a word round reverses its letters

parts.note: POWs is the abbreviation for prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Captives from each side are swapped one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant spelling: swop is a British form of swap, meaning to exchange.

clue.text: Unfortunate people were knocked down in this traffic

definitions.text: Unfortunate people were knocked down in this traffic

parts.words: Unfortunate people were knocked down in this traffic
parts.note: knocked down means sold at auction, and traffic means trade, not road vehicles

explanation.surface: Pedestrians being hit by cars on a busy road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked down' and 'traffic' suggest a road accident; at an auction an item is knocked down to a bidder, and traffic is commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: The slave trade was commerce in enslaved people, who were sold at auction.

clue.text: Two things required for a fiddle one's seen at the card table

definitions.text: one's seen at the card table

parts.words: Two things required for a fiddle
parts.note: a violin needs a bridge to hold its strings up and a person to play it

parts.words: Two things required for a fiddle
parts.note: a violin needs a bridge to hold its strings up and a person to play it

explanation.surface: A cheat needs two accomplices to rig a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests a swindle at cards; it is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game, so someone who plays it sits at the card table.

clue.text: Possibly stayed for Sunday

indicators.note: possibly signals the fodder could be arranged another way

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone stayed over until Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Sunday is traditionally the weekly day set aside for rest.

clue.text: Elegant fashion on a bride

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are formed into a new word

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A stylish outfit worn by a bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' reads as a noun about clothes; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: debonair means stylish, charming and elegant.

clue.text: Tap observed to be crooked

parts.note: a cock is a tap or valve
eyed means looked at, observed

explanation.surface: A tap that was spotted being bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cockeyed means askew or crooked.

clue.text: Fuel-saving trip that's intended to reduce overheads

definitions.meaning: a motoring run done to use as little petrol as possible
a campaign by a business to cut its costs

explanation.surface: A drive to burn less fuel, part of the firm's cost-cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is a frugal car journey and a cost-cutting campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a motoring run made to save petrol and a company push to spend less.

clue.text: He stole away from the shore

definitions.text: He stole away from the shore

parts.words: He stole away from the shore
parts.note: stole means robbed, and away from the shore means at sea

explanation.surface: A man crept off quietly from the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole away' looks like slipping off secretly; it is theft committed out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber who attacks ships at sea.

clue.text: They may be after estate — amen!

definitions.meaning: estate ... sell houses, so the word can follow estate
split as A MEN; gents is a word for men

explanation.surface: Some people may be after the property, so be it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amen' read as A MEN gives A + GENTS, since gents means men.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate agents are the people who sell property, and A GENTS is A MEN.

clue.text: Classic acorn producers

definitions.meaning: one of the five Classics, the major British flat horse races

explanation.surface: A traditional tale of trees bearing acorns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a famous English horse race run at Epsom; the five Classics are the leading races for three-year-olds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is a classic horse race, and oak trees bear acorns.

clue.text: Compensating for disappointing scenery

parts.note: off means poor, not up to standard
a setting is the scenery of a play

explanation.surface: Making amends for stage scenery that let the audience down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: offsetting something means balancing or compensating for it.

clue.text: Was its queen a graduate of Girton?

parts.note: Girton was a women's college at Cambridge, so its graduate is a female BA
Girton was a women's college at Cambridge, so its graduate is a female BA

explanation.surface: A question whether a famous queen studied at a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: Girton, a Cambridge college, was founded for women, so its graduate is SHE (a woman) with a BA degree; the queen of Sheba visited Solomon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the ancient kingdom whose queen, in the Bible, visited King Solomon.

clue.text: Save up to get a brass instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: save means except, as does but

explanation.surface: Put money aside to buy a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save up' looks like a phrase about money; 'save' is BUT (except), turned by 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the tuba is the largest, deepest instrument of the brass family.

clue.text: Military command that's withdrawn?

parts.note: a parade order cancelling a previous order, and also a way of retracting what was just said

explanation.surface: An army order that has been cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a drill order to return to the previous position, used generally to cancel what was just said.

clue.text: Arthur's head is in a drink once more

indicators.note: is in places the letter inside the drink

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Arthur has his head in a drink once again.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: again means one more time.

clue.text: Make out new plan for Marxist flotation

parts.note: red is a term for a communist or Marxist
a raft is a flotation device

explanation.surface: Drawing up a fresh scheme for a communist's floating platform.
explanation.definitionFit: Redrafting is writing out a revised version of a plan or document.

clue.text: Eternal solution for unstable sea legs

indicators.note: unstable means not settled, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: The everlasting cure for wobbly sea legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ageless means never growing old, eternal.
